title: Neuromodulation supports robust rhythmic pattern transitions in degenerate central pattern generators with fixed connectivity
summary: Many essential biological functions, such as breathing and locomotion, rely on the coordination of robust and adaptable rhythmic patterns, governed by specific network architectures known as connectomes. Rhythmic adaptation is often linked to slow structural modifications of the connectome through synaptic plasticity, but such mechanisms are too slow to support rapid, localized rhythmic transitions.
